headline: Octopuses have three hearts. ==Two of them stop== when they swim.

slides.label: The weird part
slides.heading: The main heart quits mid-swim. So octopuses ==prefer to crawl.==
slides.body: Two hearts push blood to the gills. The third serves the body, and it pauses under the strain of swimming. Crawling simply costs less energy.

slides.label: One more thing
slides.heading: Their blood is blue. Copper does the job iron does in ours.
slides.body: Octopus blood uses a copper-based molecule to carry oxygen in cold, low-oxygen water. Copper turns it blue.

caption:
An octopus would rather crawl for an hour than swim for a minute.

Swimming jets water through its body, and the pressure squeezes the main heart until it stops. Every swim is a held breath for its circulation. So evolution picked the lazy option: eight arms, low gear, crawl everywhere.

Bonus: their blood runs on copper instead of iron. That is why it is blue.
